fields.habitat: Semi-aquatic environments in South Florida, favoring the Everglades, canal banks, levees, and marshes.
fields.behavior: Cryptic ambush predator. Activity is governed by thermoregulation; detection probability in brush is below 1%.
fields.hunting_strategy: Active visual surveying (road/levee cruising) on sunny winter days or warm dusk hours. Capture using snake hooks/tongs, followed by legal two-step euthanization.

fields.habitat: Present in all 67 counties: oak-cabbage palm hammocks, pine flatwoods, marshes, and sloughs.
fields.behavior: Small sounders or solitary boars. Aggressive rooting feeders. Highly adaptable and readily turns nocturnal under hunting pressure.
fields.hunting_strategy: Night hunting over bait on private land using thermal optics/lights; swamp buggies for flooded terrain; trained bay dogs in dense brush.

fields.habitat: Edge habitats where dense timber meets open agricultural land or young ground vegetation.
fields.behavior: Crepuscular (active at dawn/dusk). Follows distinct scent trails and bedding corridors. High activity during seasonal rut cycles.
fields.hunting_strategy: Tree stands or ground blinds overlooking travel funnels or feed sources downwind. Scent control is vital; antler rattling and grunt calls during rut.

fields.title: Bag Limit Exceptions
fields.text: Deer taken on private lands under the Antlerless Deer Permit Program (antlerless deer only), Private Lands Deer Management Permit Program and Deer Depredation Permit Program and on licensed game farms and hunting preserves are excluded from bag (daily and annual) and possession limits. Any deer testing positive for CWD also is excluded from all bag limits.

fields.title: Private Land Wild Hog Regulations
fields.text: Wild hogs may be trapped and hunted year-round with landowner permission. A hunting license is not required, and a permit is not required to take wild hogs at night with a gun and light with landowner permission. Hunters may use dogs and any legal rifle, shotgun, crossbow, bow, pistol or air gun (including airbow). There is no size or bag limit, and either sex may be harvested. Wild hogs may be trapped using live traps (e.g., box traps, cage traps, corral traps). Trapped animals may not be released on public lands and may only be released on private property with landowner permission. Persons wishing to transport or hold live wild hogs must first obtain applicable permits from the Florida Department of Agriculture and Consumer Services (FDACS) . When hunting wild hogs using dogs, all dogs must wear a collar or tag that legibly displays the dog owner’s name and address. Written permission from the landowner (or lessee) is required, must be in each hunter’s possession, and must be presented for inspection upon request of any FWC wildlife officer or other law enforcement officer. In addition, all dogs not under physical restraint used for pursuing wild hog must be equipped and monitored with devices that allow remote tracking and behavior correction.

fields.title: WMA-Specific Wild Hog Regulations
fields.text: Expand All | Collapse All When wild hogs may be hunted on WMAs Expand/Collapse When wild hogs may be hunted on WMAs On most wildlife management areas (WMAs), wild hog hunting is allowed during most seasons, except spring turkey season. A hunting license is never required, but a management area permit is usually required, and a quota or daily quota permit may be required (see the area-specific WMA regulations for details). People may hunt wild hogs only during established seasons and in accordance with regulations outlined in the area-specific WMA regulations . Wild hog hunting is not allowed year-round on WMAs, except on the Kissimmee Chain of Lakes Area and the  Rolling Meadows Unit - Kissimmee Chain of Lakes Area. Wild hogs may be hunted during small-game seasons on most WMAs. Allowed methods of take for hunting wild hogs on WMAs Expand/Collapse Allowed methods of take for hunting wild hogs on WMAs During archery season, hunters may only use a bow. During muzzleloading gun season, they may only use a muzzleloading gun. During small-game season, the use of centerfire rifles is prohibited on many WMAs. However, shotguns (including the use of slugs/buckshot), rimfire rifles (including .22-magnum), revolvers, pistols, muzzleloading guns, bows, crossbows and air guns (including airbows) are usually allowed – check the area-specific WMA regulations for details. Area-specific regulations apply when hunting on WMAs, which may include restrictions on the types of allowed guns and firearms, and the use of dogs. On WMAs that allow the use of dogs to hunt wild hogs, all dogs must wear a collar or tag that legibly displays the name and address of the dog's owner. In addition, all dogs not under physical restraint used for pursuing wild hog must be equipped and monitored with devices that allow remote tracking. On July 1, 2022, such dogs must also be equipped with devices that allow for remote behavior correction. Bag limits for wild hogs on WMAs Expand/Collapse Bag limits for wild hogs on WMAs On most WMAs, there are no bag or size limits on wild hogs. However, on some WMAs, daily bag limits do apply; and on a few WMAs, there's even a minimum size limit on wild hogs. Hunters should always read the regulations brochure for the WMA they wish to hunt before going. Brochures are available online only at MyFWC.com/WMAbrochures . fields.title: Private Land Burmese Python Regulations
fields.text: Hunting on Private Land: Nonnative reptiles like Burmese pythons can be humanely killed on private lands at any time with landowner permission - no permit required- and the FWC encourages people to capture and humanely kill pythons from private lands whenever possible. There is no bag limit.

fields.title: Commission-Managed Land Burmese Python Regulations
fields.text: Hunting on Commission-managed lands: P er Executive Order 23-16, nonnative reptiles including pythons may also be humanely killed at any time throughout the year on 32 Commission-managed lands listed below. All specific provisions in Executive Order 23-16 and all area rules and  must be followed. No permit or hunting license is required. There is no bag limit.
